# M1A1 condition-finish review: D03 soot v84 and W03 halo v85

Both finishes are weak. D03's soot can be seen in only one of the views I checked, the 1000 top view. W03's halo helps the roof hole read as damage up close, but the tank still doesn't read as destroyed. My recommendation for both is **KEEP THIS FINISH DIRECTION WITH LIMITS**, and both physical directions are still useful.

This was a read-only review. I made no edits or producer calls and ran no commands. In each folder the repeat renders have the same hashes as the originals, and both manifests record `pixelsAltered:false` and `humanApproved:false`. Technical validation passed, but I don't treat that as visual clearance. Native and mask checks are still pending, not failed. These are informal observations: no scores, no formal go, no approval.

---

## D03 — damaged03-soot-v84 (job 2a2265ed…, r3, checkpoint db8d3bf5…, GLB 7a8b5bd8…)

One oddity: `original-render-evidence.json` still names the asset "engine-fire finish candidate". The relocation hashes match the brief.

### Six 256 views
| File | What I see |
|---|---|
| `256-front-three-quarter.png` | Looks clean. The rear deck is out of view, as expected. |
| `256-rear-three-quarter.png` | Two grille bays. The near bay has the darker, irregular lifted slats from v69. I can't see any soot around them. |
| `256-front.png` | Same as clean. |
| `256-left.png` | The lifted grille makes a tiny tick on the rear-deck line. No soot visible. |
| `256-right.png` | Looks clean. The feature is on the other side, so this is expected. |
| `256-top.png` | Two framed bays. The bay on the right of the image has a faint darker cast that spreads a little onto the cross plate below it. It's barely separable from v69. |

### 1000 comparisons (same camera)
- **Top.** In `soot-v84/1000-top.png` there is a soft brown-black smudge around the bent bay on the right of the image. It is heaviest at the bay and bleeds down across the cross plate. `fire-v69/1000-top.png` has the same bent bars without the smudge. `clean-desert-v1-r2/1000-top.png` has one continuous grille.
  - The smudge falls down-right of the bay, while the scene's shadows fall up-left. So it reads as a stain rather than a cast shadow.
  - It sits on the bent bay and not on the normal one, so it hangs together with the displaced grille.
  - Its edge is a uniform soft blur, so it reads as an airbrushed smudge rather than soot streaking.
- **Rear three-quarter.** I see no visible difference between `soot-v84/1000-rear-three-quarter.png` and `fire-v69/1000-rear-three-quarter.png`. The brown curled slats on the near bay are unchanged, and no soot reads on the surrounding deck. Clean has one grille.
- **Left.** v84 and v69 look identical: both have the lifted slats breaking the rear-deck line. Clean has a flat dotted deck line.

### 128 comparisons
- **Top.** `128-top.png` may be very slightly darker at the right-of-image bay than v69. That is at the edge of what I can see. Clean differs mainly because it has one grille.
- **Rear three-quarter and left.** `128-rear-three-quarter.png` and `128-left.png` look the same as v69 to me, and I can't pick out the damage at this size.

### Strongest objections
1. **The finish only shows in one view.** It reads in `1000-top.png` but not in `1000-rear-three-quarter.png`, the main oblique view of the deck. As a fire cue, it adds almost nothing over v69.
2. **The soot looks like a smudge.** The soft, even falloff reads as an airbrushed brown smudge, not soot pattern from heat leaving a vent.
3. **The grille layout still differs from clean.** The two-bay layout doesn't match the single grille on clean v1.0, as the prior findings already noted, and v84 doesn't resolve that.
4. **The slats could still read as debris.** The brown curled slats in `1000-rear-three-quarter.png` could still pass for loose material, and the soot doesn't help them read as a warped frame.
5. **Recognition is intact.** The tank reads as an M1A1 in every view, and I have no objection to its primary forms. It reads as a lightly damaged tank only from close range.

### Recommendation: **KEEP THIS FINISH DIRECTION WITH LIMITS**
The soot is harmless and in the right place, at the level of restraint the brief asked for. Limits:
- It doesn't show fire beyond the 1000 top view.
- It must not be counted as visible at 256 or 128.
- The grille-layout question still needs a decision.

**The physical direction (the bent grille) is still useful.** The prior D03 v69 findings stand, and no approval transfers.

---

## W03 — destroyed03-halo-v85 (job 6aa9acc8…, r3, checkpoint a0571752…, GLB 1c847afe…)

### Six 256 views
| File | What I see |
|---|---|
| `256-front-three-quarter.png` | A dark opening on the bustle roof next to the rail. There's a slight darker fringe, but no clear halo at this size. |
| `256-rear-three-quarter.png` | A dark opening with a hint of its inner wall. The halo isn't separable at this size. |
| `256-front.png`, `256-left.png`, `256-right.png` | Same as clean. The feature is on the roof, so this is expected. |
| `256-top.png` | A dark block with a soft gray-brown fringe on its right and top edges. It looks a little less like a flat decal than v72 did. |

### 1000 comparisons (same camera)
- **Top.** In `halo-v85/1000-top.png` there is a gray-brown halo around the cavity. It is heaviest on the right edge and the top-right corner, and fades toward the hatch. `cavity-v72/1000-top.png` has the same cavity with a crisp, clean rim. Clean has an intact roof.
  - The halo is uneven and doesn't match the shadow direction, so it reads more as scorch than shadow.
  - Its edge is a uniform soft blur with no streaks or flaking, so it also reads somewhat as a soft-paint vignette.
- **Front three-quarter.** In `halo-v85/1000-front-three-quarter.png` the rim is slightly darker than in v72, most visibly on the right lip. This helps a little against the read of a "maintenance hatch with the lid removed".
- **Rear three-quarter.** In `halo-v85/1000-rear-three-quarter.png` the rim may be a touch darker than in `cavity-v72/1000-rear-three-quarter.png`, but I can barely see a difference.
  - The cavity depth is real: the inner wall is lit and the floor is in shadow.
  - The rim is straight-edged with no torn or bent metal.
  - No broken or displaced panel can be seen.
  - Nothing floats, and the rail and antennas are seated.
- **Left.** v85 and v72 look identical, and both match clean.

### 128 comparisons
- **Top.** `halo-v85/128-top.png` and `cavity-v72/128-top.png` both show a small dark block, and I can't see a halo difference. I didn't open v72's 128 rear-three-quarter or left.
- **Rear three-quarter.** `128-rear-three-quarter.png` shows a dark speck that is nearly lost.
- **Left.** `128-left.png` looks clean.

### Analogue check (`usmc-hansen.jpg`, as a broad visual analogue only)
The photo shows blackening and paint loss across the whole turret and hull, and an ash bed at the base. v85 shows none of that: outside a roughly one-panel radius the tank is untouched tan. The halo deals only with the local rim.

### Strongest objections
1. **The tank doesn't read as destroyed.** In `1000-front-three-quarter.png`, `1000-rear-three-quarter.png` and every 256 and 128 view, it is a clean tan tank with one dark roof opening. That remains a condition gap, broader than this finish.
2. **The halo is too soft.** Its even, airbrushed falloff in `1000-top.png` could pass for a paint vignette, and it adds no fractured texture.
3. **The rupture still has no violent shape.** The straight, crisp rim and the lack of a visible broken panel, both raised in the prior W03 v72 review, are unchanged. A finish can't supply those.
4. **The finish is invisible at 128 and marginal at 256.**
5. **Recognition is intact.** I have no objection to its primary forms or materials.

### Recommendation: **KEEP THIS FINISH DIRECTION WITH LIMITS**
The local halo is a sound layer. In `1000-top.png` and `1000-front-three-quarter.png` it moves the cavity slightly toward reading as damage rather than an opened hatch. Limits:
- On its own it doesn't make the tank read as destroyed.
- Its value is limited to 1000 and the top view.
- It must not stand in for whole-vehicle condition work or for fracture geometry at the rim.

**The physical direction (the cavity) is still useful.** The prior W03 v72 physical findings stand, and no approval transfers.
